Schatzker Classification for Tibial Plateau Fractures

  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Definition

  • 6 grades classification system for tibial plateau fractures
  • It combines fracture location, pattern, fracture energy and tibial plateau involved if it is lateral or medial or both to produce this system
  • Low energy vs high energy
  • Grade (I- III) low energy
  • Grade (IV- VI) high energy
  • Unicondylar vs bicondylar
  • Grade (I- IV) unicondylar
  • Grade (V and VI) bicondylar
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Classification

  • Grade I: split fracture of the lateral tibial plateau
  • Grade II: split- depression fracture of the lateral tibial plateau
  • Grade III: depression fracture of the lateral tibial plateau
  • Grade III A: lateral depression
  • Grade III B: central depression
  • Grade IV: split or depression fracture of the medial tibial plateau
  • Grade V: wedge shape pattern fracture involving both tibial plateaus
  • Grade VI: dissociation of the articular surface from the diaphysis + any other fracture
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 1

  • Vertical split of the lateral condyle of the tibia in the sagittal plane
  • Most common in young people who have hard cancellous trabeculae and good bone density so the bone splits and doesn’t depress
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 2

  • Split- depression fracture of the lateral tibial plateau
  • Most common grade
  • Associated with either greater energy than a Grade I or with poor bone quality
  • The lateral tibial plateau can’t stand the load of the lateral femoral condyle and that is why it sustains split- depression fracture
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 3

  • Depression fracture of the lateral tibial plateau and it’s classified into two types: Grade III A with lateral depression while Grade III B with central depression of the lateral tibial plateau
  • Associated with poor bone quality and can be caused by very low energy mechanisms.
  • Most common in elderly
  • Joint stability is rarely affected but axial instability might occur with Grade III B
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 4

  • Split or split- depression fracture in the medial plateau. The fracture pass lateral to the intercondylar eminence and goes back medially to separate the medial plateau from the tibia
  • Mechanism of injury: high energy Varus force with axial loading
  • Knee joint stability is extensively affected and they represent variant of knee dislocation
  • High risk for compartment syndrome and neurovascular injury
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 5

  • Split or split- depression fracture involving both tibial plateaus. Intercondylar eminence is spared because of the cruciate ligament holding it
  • Total articular injury
  • Mechanism of injury is high energy force
  • unstable knee joint but it is more stable than Grade IV
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 6

  • dissociation of the articular surface from the diaphysis + any other fracture
  • Mechanism of injury: high energy force, open fracture with extensive soft tissue injury and compartment syndrome is common with this grade
  • Unstable knee joint
  • High risk for compartment syndrome and neurovascular injury
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden
